profile.campus: Hillsboro, Washington County, Oregon (QTS Hillsboro 2 campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own Hillsboro 2 campus page, this DC1 building sits at 4755 NE Huffman St, Hillsboro, OR 97124, part of a 51-acre, four-building (DC1/DC2/DC3/DC5) campus totaling 180+ MW of power capacity, which QTS describes as designed for rapid, large-scale Pacific Northwest deployments.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT)-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. Hillsboro, in Oregon's Washington County, is one of three QTS campuses in the immediate area (Hillsboro 1, 2, and 3) and part of the Portland metro's broader "Silicon Forest" data center cluster, drawing power from the regional grid and, per QTS's own Hillsboro 3 materials, offering customers 100% renewable energy through power purchase agreements.

Hillsboro's "Silicon Forest" data center cluster grew out of the area's legacy semiconductor and electronics manufacturing base (anchored historically by Intel's large Washington County campuses), which left behind substantial fiber infrastructure and a skilled technical workforce that later attracted data center operators; the Hillsboro Herald, a local outlet, has reported on the scale of competing data center construction projects in the immediate area as the industrial land base has shifted from chip fabrication toward digital infrastructure. QTS's Hillsboro presence, spread across three separate campuses (Hillsboro 1, 2, and 3), reflects a broader industry pattern in Oregon's Washington County of sequential campus expansion by the same operator as adjacent land becomes available, similar to the multi-campus patterns seen for QTS in Northern Virginia and for other operators in this registry's Loudoun County and Quincy, Washington clusters.

reading.body:
QTS Hillsboro 2 is a 51-acre campus in Oregon's largest data center cluster with 180 MW of published total power capacity across four buildings. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this would represent roughly 4,500 racks campus-wide, though the operator publishes no per-building breakdown and this specific facility record cannot be matched to one of the four distinct Huffman Street addresses DataCenterMap lists for the campus. The campus sits in a region with substantial incumbent capacity from Digital Realty and Verizon, and ranks ninth among the eight Oregon facilities that publish power figures to this site, suggesting either a data reporting gap across the state or that most of Oregon's mapped data center footprint operates without published specifications.

The campus's primary constraint for AI workloads is power density relative to building footprint. If all 180 MW of campus capacity were available for GPU compute, and if 40 kW per rack remains a reasonable baseline for current training hardware, available space might be the limiting factor rather than power. The operator's Blackstone ownership, following a 2021 acquisition, does not carry published commitments to any specific tenant class or AI infrastructure specialization; that information is not public.

No certification status, cooling specification, power delivery architecture, or grid interconnection detail is published for this campus. Without per-building power and space detail, and without disambiguation of which Hillsboro 2 building this record describes, this entry cannot yet support precise capacity assessment for AI scaling decisions. Resolution would require the operator to publish building-level power and square footage figures.
